subject: A single leafless canopy tree of Tabebuia impetiginosa in full magenta flower, standing clear of low dry-season woodland. Crown filling the upper two thirds of the frame, bare grey trunk below, a few fallen trumpet flowers on the ground.
A close vertical study of a mature tropical hardwood trunk: grey fissured outer bark, deep cracks, a torn edge on one side where a strip has been taken and the reddish inner layer shows through.

Seasonally dry South American woodland at the end of the dry season, seen from the ground: open spaced trees, pale bare branches, dry grass and leaf litter, with two or three magenta crowns showing in the middle distance.
A small pile of long inner-bark strips, reddish brown between cinnamon and old brick, laid along the frame with one strip pulled apart at the end into fibrous threads that run with the grain.

Curved plates of grey corky outer bark, cracked and weathered on the upper face, arranged beside a handful of pale blond square-cut sapwood chips. One bark plate snapped in half to show the granular fracture.

Shredded bark simmering in a shallow dark steel pan of reddish brown liquid, seen from just above the rim: fibres suspended and turning, a faint steam, the liquid deep enough to read its colour against the metal.
A loose mound of finely milled bark powder, warm reddish brown with visible short fibres in it, spilled from one side of the frame with a shallow scoop mark drawn through the surface.
